verses.text: After Saul died, David returned from defeating the Amalekites and spent two days in Ziklag.
On the third day a man arrived from Saul's camp with torn clothes and dirt on his head. When he reached David, he fell to the ground and bowed.
David asked, “Where have you come from?” He answered, “I escaped from Israel's camp.”
David asked, “What happened? Tell me.” He said, “Our troops ran from the battle, and many fell and died. Saul and his son Jonathan are dead too.”
David asked the young man, “How do you know Saul and Jonathan are dead?”
He said, “I happened to be on Mount Gilboa and saw Saul leaning on his spear. The chariots and horsemen were closing in on him.
He looked back, saw me, and called to me. I answered, ‘Here I am.’
He asked, ‘Who are you?’ I told him, ‘I'm an Amalekite.’
He said, ‘Come over here and kill me, please. I'm in agony, and I'm still alive.’
So I went over and killed him because I was sure he wouldn't survive after what had happened. I took the crown from his head and the bracelet from his arm and brought them here to you, my lord.”
David grabbed his clothes and tore them, and all the men with him did the same.
They mourned, wept, and fasted until evening for Saul and Jonathan, for the LORD's people, and for the house of Israel, because they'd fallen by the sword.
David asked the young man who brought him the news, “Where are you from?” He said, “I'm the son of a foreigner, an Amalekite.”
David asked, “Why weren't you afraid to raise your hand against the LORD's anointed and kill him?”
David called one of his young men and told him to strike the messenger down. The man struck him, and he died.
David said, “Your blood is on your own head. Your own words testified against you when you said, ‘I killed the LORD's anointed.’”
David sang this lament for Saul and his son Jonathan.
He told the people to teach the children of Judah the Song of the Bow, which is written in the Book of Jashar.
“Israel, your glory lies slain on your heights. How the mighty have fallen!
Don't tell it in Gath or announce it in the streets of Ashkelon. The daughters of the Philistines will celebrate, and the daughters of the uncircumcised will shout for joy.
Mountains of Gilboa, may no dew or rain fall on you and no fields yield offerings. There the mighty man's shield was defiled and cast away. Saul's shield lies without its oil.
From the blood of the fallen and the fat of the mighty, Jonathan's bow never turned back. Saul's sword never came home empty.
Saul and Jonathan were loved and admired in life, and death didn't separate them. They were faster than eagles and stronger than lions.
Daughters of Israel, weep for Saul. He dressed you in fine scarlet and put gold ornaments on your clothes.
How the mighty have fallen in the middle of battle! Jonathan lies slain on your heights.
I'm grieving for you, Jonathan, my brother. You were so dear to me. Your love for me was wonderful, beyond the love of women.
How the mighty have fallen, and the weapons of war have perished!”
